floor_history.headline: Floor 27 -> 15 and build_insns now exactly 109 = target: copying the matched, user-authorized GTE-LZC island from the same-file sibling func_800274BC fixed a 12-point cheat-classifier artifact; the en

frontier.hypothesis: The residual 15 closes in one step if the record-walker pseudo is allocated LAST of the three rotating values ($a3) instead of first ($a1) — mflo1 then falls into $a1 and ent into $a2.
frontier.mechanism: global.c find_reg scans hard regs in the default ascending order (no REG_ALLOC_ORDER in mips.h); allocnos are served in priority order, priority driven by live_length * n_refs. Lowering the walker's priority below ent's reorders the three assignments as a unit.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run tmp/grind/func_80032314/s1/greg.sh, but read the ALLOCNO PRIORITY ORDER rather than only the final dispositions — use the BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG instrumented cc1 at tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 (the TOP-LEVEL cc1, not build/cc1, per [[instrumented-cc1-location]]) to print the sorted allocno list, get the actual ranking of pseudos 74 / 75 / 115, then choose the C edit that swaps exactly the walker's and ent's ranks.

frontier.hypothesis: Re-deriving the `+2` walker view inside the loop body (instead of hoisting it across the whole loop) shortens its live range enough to drop it below ent in allocno priority.
frontier.mechanism: Same global.c priority = live_length * n_refs. A shorter live range lowers priority without changing the emitted instructions IF the loop optimizer strength-reduces the per-iteration derivation back to the target's single `addiu $a3,$t0,0x2` prologue insn plus single `addiu $a3,$a3,0x2C` latch insn.
frontier.next_probe: Declare `u8 *w = t0 + 2;` inside the loop body after the `*t0 == 0` guard, drop the hoisted walker, and FIRST confirm build_insns is still 109 before reading the score — an insn-count change means the strength-reducer did not fold it and the variant is invalid regardless of score.

frontier.hypothesis: Raising `ent`'s reference count byte-neutrally lifts it above the walker in allocno priority and resolves the rotation without touching the walker at all.
frontier.mechanism: The duplicated-statement-into-arms family (.claude/rules/duplicated-statement-into-arms.md) is the documented byte-free reg_n_refs lift for exactly this class of global-RA priority wall; jump2 cross-jump re-merges the duplicate so the emitted bytes are unchanged.
frontier.next_probe: ONLY after the two probes above are measured: duplicate the `*(s16 *)(ent + 0x286) = 5;` store (or the `ent + 0x6A` read) into both arms of the `log2_val < v0` test, verify build_insns stays 109 (byte-neutrality), read the score.
